content: Community Health Workers (CHWs) are individuals who are deeply trusted within the communities they serve. They act as a vital link between healthcare systems and populations that are often underserved or face barriers to accessing care. Their responsibilities include conducting outreach efforts to engage community members, advocating for the needs and rights of individuals within the community, and providing social support to those who require assistance. They also facilitate referrals to appropriate healthcare services when necessary. In certain situations, CHWs may carry out specific clinical tasks, but only under the direct supervision of licensed healthcare professionals.
